question: Does covariance tell you whether one variable causes the other?
direct_answer: No. Covariance only shows association, not causation.
expanded_answer: Two variables can have high covariance because they share a common cause, because of a direct relationship, or even by coincidence in finite data. Covariance alone does not identify direction, mechanism, or causal effect.
key_points: A third variable can explain the relationship
common_wrong_ideas: If covariance is positive, one variable causes the other
If covariance is zero, there is no relationship of any kind
